items.q: How do you protect our IP before a factory ever sees a drawing?
items.a: We'll sign an NDA before any detailed disclosure on our side. Once a factory is involved, an NNN agreement is executed before drawings or spec sheets are shared, and disclosure is staged so tooling partners see only what they need to manufacture.

items.q: What happens if a production run comes back off spec?
items.a: It doesn't ship. Every run is checked against AQL sampling standards before it leaves the factory; units outside the agreed defect threshold are reworked or rejected at the factory's cost, per terms set before production started.

items.q: We only have a rough sketch. Can you still help?
items.a: Yes, that's the normal starting point. Concept and industrial design is the first phase of the engagement, not a prerequisite for it.

items.q: What's a realistic budget, and how is CUSTOM+ priced?
items.a: It depends on category, tooling complexity, and volume. Injection molded parts typically carry a higher minimum order quantity (MOQ) than CNC or sheet metal parts because of tooling amortization. Design and engineering are scoped per phase; production and logistics are priced against the factory quotes we negotiate on your behalf, with our fee disclosed separately, never buried inside a marked up unit cost.

items.q: How long does a typical project take?
items.a: From first brief through the first sample round is usually 9 to 19 weeks depending on tooling complexity, with production and logistics adding 7 to 14 weeks on top. Simple products move faster; anything with tight tolerances takes the time it takes to get right.

items.q: How do you handle compliance like CE, FCC, or RoHS?
items.a: Certification requirements are identified during design, not discovered after tooling. We coordinate testing with accredited labs for the markets you ship to and build the timeline into the production schedule.

items.q: How is this different from a sourcing agent?
items.a: A sourcing agent finds you a factory and steps back. We stay through design, tooling, every sample round, production QC, and freight, paid to represent your interests, not to move volume for a factory.

items.q: Do you work with brands that already have a factory?
items.a: Yes, sometimes the fix is design and QC oversight on an existing relationship, not a new factory. We'll tell you honestly which one your situation needs.

redflag.kicker: Already have a quote from somewhere else?
redflag.heading: Stress test it. Six checks, no upload, thirty seconds.
redflag.lead: These are the standard safeguards we check for on every quote we review, including ones that were never going to be ours.

questions.question: Does it separate tooling cost from unit price?
Is the mold cavity count specified?
Are payment terms staged, not 100% upfront?
Is there a written IP or NNN clause?
Does it specify an AQL or inspection standard?
Is tooling ownership stated in writing?

explanations.tooling: Vague tooling versus unit pricing is a classic place a markup hides. Ask for tooling and unit cost as two separate lines.
explanations.cavity: Without a stated cavity count, you can not verify the per unit price makes sense at your volume.
explanations.payment: 100% upfront removes your only real leverage if quality drops after the sample.
explanations.ip: No NNN clause means nothing formally stops the factory from reproducing or reselling your design.
explanations.aql: No inspection standard means "good enough" gets decided after the fact, not agreed in advance.
explanations.ownership: Unclear tooling ownership can mean starting over, and paying again, if you ever switch factories.
